Converted 1850s townhouses on the same strip where Louis Armstrong learned to play his trumpet. 

Unlike many other 2-, 3-, and 4-bedroom units, each unit at the Mary Beth spans 2-3 floors, providing enhanced privacy more suitable for stays with multiple guests traveling together.

Your unit will feature 30+ works for sale from New Orleanian poets, visual artists, and photographers. 

11 works from Son of a Ghost: collaborative works that include Mary Beth’s originals inside a lightbox along with son Robert X Fogarty’s letters to her and stories from childhood.

name: Walker’s Delight on Queen Anne
address: 11 West McGraw St,  Seattle, Washington, United States
description:
Built in 1907, this stunning six-bedroom, 2.5-bath home is nestled in the heart of the vibrant Queen Anne neighborhood, boasting an impressive walkability score of 96. Just steps from your front door, you’ll find a local wine shop, butcher, and fish market, along with convenient access to bus routes 2, 3, and 13—perfect for exploring Seattle. A Vietnamese restaurant is next door, and the pick-up point for buses on Queen Anne Avenue North (“the Ave”) is right there, offering $2.75 one-way fares ($1 for seniors). Downtown Seattle and Pike Place Market are just an 11-minute ride away, with even quicker access to the Space Needle and Chihuly Garden and Glass.
This spacious home is great for large groups, multifamily events, cruise travelers, or wedding parties looking for comfort and convenience.

Dining & Amenities at Your Doorstep
Queen Anne Avenue is lined with fantastic dining options, including How to Cook a Wolf, Eden Hill, Grappa (Italian), Ikiiki (Asian), Bounty Kitchen, Orrapin (Thai), Hilltop Alehouse, Queen Anne Café, and El Mezcalito (Mexican). Coffee lovers will appreciate being within a block of Café Ladro, Café Hagen, and Starbucks. A Safeway with pharmacy is just around the corner, with Trader Joe’s a block further. The seasonal Farmer’s Market and even more restaurants and pizza spots are a short walk away.

Neighborhood Highlights
Take a scenic walk along the “Crown of Queen Anne” loop to enjoy stunning views of the Space Needle, downtown, and Puget Sound from Kerry Park. Continue along to Marshall Park for views of Magnolia, the marina, and the waterfront, passing grand homes and a charming 1930s stone wall and lit walkway.

The Ironworks Building is a reimagined and newly renovated warehouse which combines modern comfort with classic New Orleans charm. Stallone’s The Expendables was also shot in the building, which still houses film-inspired murals bearing the autographs of Sylvester Stallone and Mickey Rourke—we challenge you to find them all!
